subtopic: Evaluating Fund Managers and Performance History
source_evidence: Many alternative mutual funds have limited performance histories. Learn as much as you can about the fund manager, such as how long he or she has managed the fund and his or her prior management or professional experience.
answer: When evaluating an alternative mutual fund, consider both its performance history and its manager’s experience. A short track record may not show how the fund would perform in a down market; many alternative funds began after 2008. Also look into how long the manager has run the fund and their prior management or professional experience. The fund’s prospectus includes certain information about the manager.
